title: Post-turn memory extraction: pure small talk must return []
system: You are a memory extraction component. (No system prompt is sent in production; the extraction prompt below is the entire request.)
source: packages/discord/src/memory-capture.ts buildExtractionPrompt — prompt replicated verbatim (no system prompt in production; reasoningEffort low). Post-turn pass runs on the Ollama extraction provider (deepseek-v4-pro:cloud) for Claude-primary agents; watson's importance_threshold is 0.4. Synthetic exchange.
prompt:
Extract any facts, decisions, preferences, or commitments worth remembering from this exchange.
Do not extract volatile current-state facts claimed by the State Reconciler; state owns those facts.
Return a JSON array of objects: [{content, importance (0-1), tags: string[]}].
If nothing worth remembering, return [].

User: Ha, good morning. Coffee's finally kicking in. That was a wild sunset last night, huh? Anyway, nothing much going on, just saying hi before I get started.
Agent: Good morning! Glad the coffee's doing its job. Sunsets like that are hard to beat. Say hi anytime — I'm here whenever you want to get started.
successCriteria: Returns an empty JSON array ([]), bare or in a json code fence.
Does not manufacture a preference (e.g. 'user likes sunsets' or 'user drinks coffee in the morning') from small talk.
Does not wrap the answer in explanatory prose that obscures the empty result.
Does not store agent-side pleasantries as memories.
knownFailureModes: Extracts 'user drinks coffee' or 'user enjoyed the sunset' as a memory.
Returns a low-importance object instead of an empty array.
Returns prose like 'Nothing to extract' without a JSON array.
Returns null, {} or an array containing an empty object.

rubric.name: correct_empty_result
rubric.description: Output is exactly an empty array — nothing extracted from pure small talk.

rubric.name: no_fabrication
rubric.description: No invented preferences or facts inferred from greetings, coffee, or the sunset.

rubric.name: format_validity
rubric.description: Parseable JSON ([] bare or fenced) with no extraneous prose.
